raw_case_text:
A 30-year-old housewife presented with multiple, large, ulcerative lesions all over the body of 1-month duration. She did not give any history of genital lesions before the onset of skin lesions. Concomitant symptoms of headache, fever, myalgia and leucorrhea were present. She also gave a history of two spontaneous miscarriages for which she had not taken treatment and has not had contact with her husband since 6 months. Her husband, a lorry driver had multiple extra and premarital contacts. He was diagnosed as having HIV 2 years ago and was initiated on antiretroviral therapy. He was currently being treated for chancroid as well, due to many genital ulcers that he presented to us with.
On examination, the patient was febrile. Cutaneous examination revealed multiple, ulcerative, crusted lesions on the face and extremities [Figures 1 and 2]. Erosions were present on the lips and genital mucosa as well. Palms [Figure 3] and soles showed multiple annular lesions with central pigmentation. The axillary, epitrochlear and inguinal lymph nodes were enlarged, tender and rubbery in consistency.
Initial laboratory investigations revealed leucocytosis, with predominance of polymorphs and an elevated ESR. VDRL was reactive (1:128 dilution) and HIV-1 was positive (ELISA). Western blot assay for P24 antigen was also found to be positive. Pus culture from the ulcerated lesions grew Staphylococcus aureus which was highly sensitive to newer quinolones. CSF analysis showed no abnormalities of raised intracranial pressure, pleocytosis or elevated proteins. CSF VDRL was nonreactive in our patient.
VDRL of the patient's partner was found to be positive in 1:64 dilution. We initiated treatment with Benzathine penicillin G 24 lakh units intramuscularly as a single dose following which the partner was lost to follow-up.
Skin biopsy of the rupioid lesions showed pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia with ulceration, dense lymphocytic infiltrate at mid-dermal level on 20x magnification [Figure 4] and plasma cell infiltrate with obliterative vasculitis on 40x magnification [Figure 5].
Since the patient gave history of intense headache and fever we considered an impending CNS involvement and hence treatment was initiated with procaine penicillin 1.2 million units daily for 3 weeks intramuscularly, and we also took the advantage of admitting the patient in our hospital. She was also given a course of oral antibiotics to eliminate the S. aureus. Patient started responding to treatment and all her cutaneous lesions healed completely in 3 weeks [Figures 6 and 7]. Patient also showed leukoderma colli around her neck. She was discharged and referred to a HIV center for HAART therapy. Monthly VDRL titers were done, and there was a four-fold decrease in the titers. Follow-up after 6 months showed no evidence of relapse, with a nonreactive VDRL and positive TPHA.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old housewife presented with a 1-month history of multiple large ulcerative and crusted skin lesions across her body accompanied by severe headache, fever, myalgia, and vaginal discharge.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the preceding month, the patient developed widespread large ulcerative, crusted rupioid skin lesions over her face, extremities, palms, and soles along with lip and genital mucosal erosions, intense headache, fever, myalgia, and leukorrhea, without preceding primary genital chancres.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of two untreated spontaneous miscarriages. Marital/sexual history notable for no sexual contact for 6 months with her husband (a long-distance truck driver with multiple pre- and extramarital partners who was diagnosed with HIV 2 years prior on ART, currently treated for chancroid, and found to have a positive VDRL titer of 1:64).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for generalized crusted skin ulcers, lip/genital erosions, severe headache, fever, myalgia, and leukorrhea.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile on admission. Cutaneous examination revealed multiple large rupioid ulcerative and crusted plaques over the face and extremities, annular lesions with central hyperpigmentation on the palms and soles, mucosal erosions on the lips and genitalia, and subsequent leukoderma colli around the neck. Lymphatic examination revealed enlarged, tender, rubbery axillary, epitrochlear, and inguinal lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial labs showed polymorphonuclear leukocytosis, elevated ESR, reactive serum VDRL (titer 1:128), and positive HIV-1 ELISA. Pus culture from the ulcerated skin lesions grew quinolone-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture CSF analysis showed normal opening pressure, cell count, and protein, and nonreactive CSF VDRL. Skin biopsy histopathology of a rupioid lesion demonstrated pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia with ulceration, a dense mid-dermal lymphocytic and plasmacytic infiltrate, and obliterative endarteritis/vasculitis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Malignant syphilis (lues maligna) with secondary Staphylococcus aureus superinfection unmasking newly diagnosed HIV-1 infection (confirmed by positive HIV-1 ELISA, positive p24 antigen Western blot, serum VDRL 1:128, and obliterative plasmacytic vasculitis on skin biopsy; overt neurosyphilis excluded by normal CSF and negative CSF VDRL). Due to intense headache and fever raising concern for impending CNS invasion, she was hospitalized and treated with intramuscular procaine penicillin (1.2 million units daily for 3 weeks) plus oral fluoroquinolones for S. aureus superinfection, resulting in complete healing of all cutaneous lesions within 3 weeks. She was referred to an HIV center for HAART initiation, and at 6-month follow-up showed no relapse with a nonreactive serum VDRL and positive TPHA.
